PrivacyText:
FreeTune privacy policy
Updated: November 25, 2026

Developer: Андреев Дмитрий
Contact: pro100dimka.and@gmail.com

With your permission, the microphone is used for tuning and recording performances. The tuner processes audio on the device without saving it. Performance recording starts only when you press Record and is stored locally. You can listen to, delete or export takes using the system file dialog. The app does not send audio to the developer. Exporting to cloud storage is subject to the selected provider’s policy. Permission can be revoked in device settings.

Songs, preferences and recently opened songs are stored locally. No developer server collects them. Songs can be deleted from the library; uninstalling the app removes its local data. Library recovery after uninstalling is not guaranteed.

The app contains no advertising or analytics SDKs. Opening a user-added YouTube video or external link may allow that service to receive your IP address, device information and process cookies under its own policy. Google privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy.

Voluntary purchases are processed by the App Store or Google Play. The app receives product and transaction status information to finish the purchase. The developer does not receive your payment card details. Store policies: https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/ and https://policies.google.com/privacy.

If you email the developer, your email address and message are used to respond and resolve your request, then deleted when no longer needed unless retention is legally required. You can request deletion of correspondence at the address above. Policy updates are published in the app.

Library backups include songs, covers and song preferences, but not audio recordings. Export important recordings separately. The embedded YouTube player loads only after you choose to show videos. Loading the player can send network information before playback starts. Its wrapper page is hosted on GitHub Pages; GitHub and YouTube may receive network information under their policies. GitHub privacy policy: https://docs.github.com/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement.

When identifying a song, an excerpt of up to 20 seconds is processed on the device and its audio fingerprint is sent to Shazam. The audio excerpt itself is not sent by this request. Song title and artist are sent to Cifra Club (cifraclub.com), E-Chords (e-chords.com), Cifras (cifras.com.br), GuitareTab (guitaretab.com), Akkords.pro (akkords.pro), Musicaccord.ru (musicaccord.ru), Chords & Tabs (chords-and-tabs.net), Sonidos (sonidos.com.br), WeingGuitar (guitar.weingchicken.com), Akkords.fun (akkords.fun), LalaTracker (lalatracker.com), LRCLIB, Пісенник (pisennyk.com.ua) and, when needed, lyrics.ovh to find lyrics and chords. Song title and artist may also be sent to SongBPM (songbpm.com) to retrieve tempo. Artwork is requested from the image URL returned by recognition. These services receive your IP address and network information. Retrieved lyrics, artwork and source links are saved on the device only when you save the song.

Phone audio capture starts only after system confirmation. On Android, only audio is read. On iOS, the system broadcast provides screen and audio buffers; FreeTune discards video and microphone buffers and temporarily stores only a bounded audio excerpt on the device for recognition. The temporary excerpt is deleted after processing or cancellation; interrupted excerpts are removed on the next recognition launch. Audio is not uploaded. Some apps prevent capture.

virtualGuitar.title: Play the virtual guitar
virtualGuitar.summary: Tap or sweep the strings to play without a physical guitar.
steps: Open Play and tap a chord. Tap a string for a single note or sweep across several strings for a strum. Both directions and multiple fingers work.
Tap + to add a chord to the sequence. Hold a chord to remove it.
Open Pattern, set BPM and tap a beat or an & cell to assign a chord change. A dot continues the previous chord. Press Play to loop the pattern while playing the strings yourself.

The metronome button works on its own. When enabled, Play starts it with the pattern; Pause stops both and remembers your choice. The fingering button chooses a chord shape. Tapping another chord changes it immediately without resetting the pulse.
Use the note button to choose a fret for each string in Free play. Close the panel and tap the strings to try a melody.
virtualGuitar.tip: The microphone and internet are not needed. Leaving the screen or locking the phone stops playback.
virtualGuitar.keywords: virtual guitar play strings melody strum picking chords bpm

start.title: Start playing
start.summary: Add a song, tune the guitar and open its chords.
steps: In Library, tap + and choose manual entry, recognition or TXT/ChordPro.
Review the artist, title, cover and text, then save.
Open the song. Tap a chord to choose its fingering, or open the gear for strumming and practice.
start.tip: Tune each string before playing. Recognition needs internet; saved songs do not.

guitar.title: Tune a guitar string
guitar.summary: The selected tuning determines the target note of each string.
steps: Allow microphone access and choose Guitar with the tuner switch.
Use Auto to detect the string, or tap a string for manual selection and its reference sound.
Play one string, mute the others and adjust it slowly until the indicator is centred and green.
guitar.tip: Yellow means closer, red means farther away. Media volume controls the reference sound.
guitar.keywords: guitar string auto manual red yellow green

chromatic.title: Use the chromatic tuner
chromatic.summary: Detect any note without restricting recognition to guitar strings.
steps: Switch to Chromatic, then play or sing one steady note.
Follow the detected note, octave, measured frequency and centred indicator.
The wave button switches waveform/spectrum; the speaker plays the note selected on the note strip.
chromatic.tip: Octave Auto detects the octave. Choose a fixed octave when needed and return to Auto to reset.
chromatic.keywords: chromatic note octave spectrum waveform speaker

calibration.title: Set the reference pitch
calibration.summary: Calibration changes which frequency the chromatic tuner considers correct.
steps: In Chromatic, tap the tuning-fork button.
Choose 432, 440 or 442 Hz, or enter a value from 400 to 480 Hz and apply.
Use the speaker to hear a selected reference note. With Octave Auto, playback uses octave 4.
calibration.tip: 440 Hz is the usual A4 reference. This calibration applies to chromatic mode, not guitar tuning presets.

tunings.title: Change the guitar tuning
tunings.summary: Use standard tuning, a preset or your own string notes.
steps: In Guitar mode, open the tuning button.
Choose a preset and check all six note labels.
For custom tuning, set each string note and save the tuning.
tunings.tip: Verify the tuning before turning the pegs. A different preset changes the target notes.
tunings.keywords: tuning standard drop open custom six strings

add.title: Add a song
add.summary: All four entry methods are under one plus button in Library.
steps: Tap + beside the search field.
Choose manual entry, microphone recognition, audio-file recognition or TXT/ChordPro.
Review the form, change the cover by tapping it and save.
add.tip: Artist comes before song title. The save button stays available while you scroll the form.
add.keywords: add plus manual cover artist title

recognize.title: Recognize with the microphone
recognize.summary: Identify the original recording, then search for available text and chords.
steps: In Library, tap +, choose microphone recognition and allow microphone access.
Tap the large listening button and play a clear original recording nearby.
When a song card appears, tap anywhere on it to open the prepared form; review and save.

Allow audio capture in the system dialog, then return to your music app. After up to 20 seconds, open FreeTune for the result. Some players do not allow audio capture. Tap Start, then the broadcast button and Start Broadcast. Return to your music app, let it play for 20 seconds, then open FreeTune. Audio from protected players may be unavailable.
recognize.tip: The first attempt is after about 3 seconds. Difficult matches can take up to 20 seconds. A match does not guarantee lyrics or chords.

audioFile.title: Recognize an audio file
audioFile.summary: Choose an existing recording instead of using the microphone.
steps: Tap + in Library and choose audio-file recognition.
Select an audio file in the system picker and wait for recognition and content lookup.
The editing form opens with the information that was found. Review it before saving.
audioFile.tip: This identifies a released recording. It does not transcribe your own performance or extract chords directly from audio.
audioFile.keywords: audio file mp3 wav recognize import recording

import.title: Import TXT or ChordPro
import.summary: Bring in a prepared song document without retyping it.
steps: Tap + in Library and choose Open TXT / ChordPro.
Choose a TXT, PRO, CHO or CHORDPRO file.
Check the imported artist, title and text. Inline chord markers are moved above the lyrics; save the song.
import.tip: Metadata can only be filled when it exists in the file. UTF-8 preserves accented letters.
import.keywords: txt chordpro pro cho import encoding

editing.title: Edit a song comfortably
editing.summary: Edit metadata, cover, links and lyrics in one form.
steps: Fill in artist and song title; tap the cover or pencil to change the image.
Open Video and links to add links. Tap the expand icon beside the text to edit full-screen.
Keep chords on a separate line above the words. Close the full-screen editor, then save.
editing.tip: Closing the full-screen editor returns to the same draft. Save the song to keep changes in the library.
editing.keywords: editing text full screen notebook cover links artist

library.title: Find and manage library songs
library.summary: Search saved songs and organize favourites.
steps: Type a title or artist in the search field.
Use the filter button to choose All, Recent or Favourites.
Hold a song card to open its menu: add/remove favourite or delete. Tap normally to open it.
library.tip: The library search looks through saved songs. Use + and recognition to identify a new recording.
library.keywords: library search filters recent favourites hold delete

reading.title: Read and scroll a song
reading.summary: Keep the lyrics visible while you play.
steps: Open a song; its chords appear above the words.
Tap the double-down-arrow auto-scroll button to start scrolling; tap again to pause.
Open the gear and Reading to adjust text size, scroll speed, transposition and capo.
reading.tip: Auto-scroll moves the text. It does not start strumming audio.
reading.keywords: reading auto scroll speed font transpose capo

chords.title: Choose and hear a fingering
chords.summary: Preview different fretboard positions for the same chord.
steps: Tap a highlighted chord above a lyric line.
Tap a fingering diagram to hear it and select it for this song. Browse other pages with the arrows.
Dots mark fretted strings, a circle means open and a cross means do not play. Close the window to return.
chords.tip: The displayed fret number is the starting fret of a higher position. Capo settings affect playback.
chords.keywords: chord fingering diagram position open mute barre preview

rhythm.title: Guitar patterns
rhythm.summary: Choose a strumming or fingerpicking pattern for the whole song or a section.
steps: Open the song gear and select Guitar patterns.
Choose Whole song or a section heading, then Strumming or Fingerpicking. Preview a card and select it with the check button.
Add Verse:, Chorus: and other section headings in the song text. Assign each its pattern or reset it to the whole-song pattern.
Practice switches patterns in song order, one bar per chord. B selects a playable bass; numbered steps pick individual strings.
rhythm.tip: Six-note 6/8 and waltz 3/4 patterns have different pulse groupings. Check the meter on the card. Explicit source patterns can be imported; ambiguous or image-only instructions stay manual.
rhythm.keywords: rhythm strum down up muted rest tempo meter preview choose fingerpicking arpeggio verse chorus section перебор перебір куплет припев приспів

practice.title: Practise chord changes
practice.summary: Practice follows the chord sequence in your song.
steps: Open the song's gear and select Practice.
Choose a comfortable tempo and starting chord.
Start the one-minute exercise and change chords with the guitar. Slow down if changes are difficult.
practice.tip: You need actual chord symbols in the song. Lyrics alone cannot create a chord exercise.
practice.keywords: practice transitions minute tempo sequence start

easier.title: Find an easier way to play
easier.summary: Try alternate chord shapes and capo positions.
steps: Open the gear, Reading, then Play easier.
Review the suggested capo position and chord shapes, then apply a suitable option.
Try the result. Use Undo if you prefer the previous position.
easier.tip: Capo fret, displayed chord shapes and transposition are different settings. Check all three when playing with a recording.
easier.keywords: easy simplify capo position undo transpose

record.title: Record a performance
record.summary: Capture singing or guitar with automatic sound processing.
steps: Open a saved song and tap its microphone/recording icon.
Tap the red button and allow microphone access. Auto-scroll starts with recording.
Tap Stop, wait until processing finishes and listen to the take in this song's recordings.
record.tip: Use headphones and avoid very loud input. Processing is automatic; this is not a separate effects editor.
record.keywords: record microphone effects processing stop auto scroll

takes.title: Play, export or delete takes
takes.summary: Each recording belongs to its song.
steps: Open the song's recording window to see its takes.
Use Play to listen. Use Export/Save file and choose a location in the system dialog.
Delete unwanted takes with the delete control. Wait if a take is still processing.
takes.tip: Library backups do not include audio takes. Export important recordings separately.
takes.keywords: takes recordings export save share delete processing

backup.title: Create a library backup
backup.summary: Protect songs and preferences before reinstalling or changing phones.
steps: Open Settings and Library backup.
Choose Save backup file and select a destination in the system dialog.
Keep a copy in a safe folder or cloud storage you can access later.
Large libraries are split automatically into numbered JSON files of up to 5 MiB. Save every part when the system dialog opens.
backup.tip: Backups include songs, artwork and song preferences. Export audio recordings separately.
backup.keywords: backup library copy transfer reinstall artwork

restore.title: Restore a backup
restore.summary: Import a FreeTune library backup into the app.
steps: Open Settings and Library backup, then Open backup.
Choose the backup file and review the restoration information.
Confirm, wait for completion and check Library.
For a multi-part backup, restore every numbered file. Each part includes its songs, artwork and preferences.
restore.tip: Save a backup of the current library first. TXT documents and audio files are not library backups.
restore.keywords: restore backup import json library merge

privacy.title: Use the app offline
privacy.summary: Saved songs and local audio functions work without internet.
steps: Tune, read saved songs, preview chords, practise and use this guide offline.
Recognition, online lyric/chord lookup and online artwork need a connection.
Read the current privacy policy in Settings for details about network requests.
privacy.tip: Recognition sends an audio fingerprint. Lyric lookup uses title and artist. Back up local data before uninstalling.
privacy.keywords: offline internet privacy fingerprint data permissions

language.title: Choose the interface language
language.summary: The first launch uses a supported language from your phone.
steps: Open Settings and Language.
Search for a language by its name and choose an available translation.
The interface and guide use the selected language. The setting is saved for future launches.
language.tip: Only complete available translations can be selected. A language listed as planned is not translated yet.
language.keywords: language translation english russian ukrainian search phone

noLyrics.title: Song identified, but chords are missing
noLyrics.summary: Recognition and lyrics with chords use different catalogs.
steps: Check that the recognized title and artist are correct.
A source may contain only lyrics, lack this song, be unavailable or block requests. Other connected sources are tried automatically.
Use Search for chords again to retry the identified song without recording again. Only a result with lyrics and chords opens as a prepared song.
noLyrics.tip: The faint Am/C example in an empty editor is a placeholder, not the recognized song. Missing chords are not invented.
noLyrics.keywords: no lyrics chords not found jimmy friday may 14 placeholder lrclib guitaretab

noMic.title: The microphone cannot hear me
noMic.summary: Check permission, input routing and other audio apps.
steps: Allow microphone access for FreeTune in the phone settings.
Close other recording apps and check whether Bluetooth or a headset is using another microphone.
For tuning, play one string. For recognition, play an original released recording clearly nearby.
noMic.tip: The tuner measures pitch. Recognition identifies a recording; singing a melody is not a reliable substitute.
noMic.keywords: microphone permission no input tuner recognition headset

noSound.title: No sound or delayed sound
noSound.summary: Check the media output before changing app settings.
steps: Raise media volume and check Bluetooth headphones or speakers.
Tap a tuner string, chord diagram or rhythm play button. The auto-scroll button only scrolls text.
If the issue persists, reopen the app and tell support your phone model, audio output and the exact screen.
noSound.tip: Bluetooth can add audible delay. Compare with the phone speaker or wired headphones; startup preparation can also take time.
noSound.keywords: sound delay latency quiet volume bluetooth string chord
